short-term-detraining.short: Detraining from under 4 weeks of too little training. In trained athletes it mostly costs blood volume, and with it VO₂max.

long-term-detraining.short: Detraining from more than 4 weeks of too little training. Losses inside the muscle (fewer mitochondria, less oxygen taken from the blood) add to the early blood losses.

retraining.short: Training again after a break, to win back what detraining took away.

muscle-memory.short: The idea that a muscle trained before keeps something that makes it respond faster when training starts again after a break.

reduced-training.short: Training less (fewer, shorter or easier sessions) instead of stopping, to keep what training built.

cross-training.short: Training in another sport to keep fitness, e.g. cycling or pool running for an injured runner.

deep-water-running.short: Running movements in deep water with a float belt, feet off the pool floor. There is no impact, so injured runners can keep training.
